reading.title: The Evolution of Renewable Energy
reading.passage: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power have become increasingly important in addressing climate change and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. Over the past decade, technological advancements have significantly reduced the cost of solar panels and wind turbines, making them more accessible to developing nations. Countries like Denmark and Costa Rica have successfully integrated renewable energy into their national grids, generating over 80% of their electricity from sustainable sources. This transition demonstrates that renewable energy is not only environmentally beneficial but also economically viable for long-term energy security.

questions.q: According to the passage, what has made renewable energy more accessible to developing nations?
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'technological advancements have significantly reduced the cost of solar panels and wind turbines'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 기술 발전이 개발도상국에 신재생에너지를 더 접근 가능하게 만들었습니다.

questions.q: Which countries are mentioned as examples of successful renewable energy integration?
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'Countries like Denmark and Costa Rica have successfully integrated renewable energy'라고 직접 언급되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred about the future of renewable energy?
options: It will replace all fossil fuels immediately
It is economically and environmentally viable for the future
It is too expensive for most countries
It cannot be integrated into existing grids
questions.explanation: 본문의 마지막 문장 'renewable energy is not only environmentally beneficial but also economically viable for long-term energy security'에서 신재생에너지의 긍정적인 미래 전망을 추론할 수 있습니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the statement: 'Remote work is more productive than working in an office environment'?

structure.intro: 명확한 입장 표현하기: 'I agree/disagree because...' 또는 'In my opinion, remote work is/is not more productive because...'로 시작하여 주요 이유를 간단히 제시
structure.body1: 첫 번째 이유 발전시키기: 구체적인 예시나 증거 제시 (집중력 향상, 출퇴근 시간 단축 등)
structure.body2: 두 번째 이유 발전시키기: 상반된 관점도 언급하면서 자신의 입장 강화 (협업의 어려움 vs 자율성 증가 등)
structure.conclusion: 앞의 주장들을 요약하고 최종 결론 도출: 'In conclusion, remote work is beneficial because...'

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer spending leisure time outdoors with friends. Others prefer indoor activities like watching movies or reading. Which do you prefer and why?
useful_expressions: In my opinion, I prefer outdoor activities because...
One reason is that spending time outside helps me relax and stay healthy.
sample_points: 야외활동의 건강상 이점: 신선한 공기, 신체활동, 스트레스 해소 등을 구체적으로 설명
친구와의 상호작용 강화: 야외에서 더 자연스러운 대화와 깊은 유대관계 형성 가능성 강조

listening.title: Study Habits Discussion
listening.script: Professor: Good afternoon, Sarah. How are your studies progressing this semester? Sarah: Hi Professor. Honestly, I've been struggling to balance my classes and part-time job. I'm finding it hard to concentrate on my assignments. Professor: I understand. Many students face this challenge. Have you considered using the library's study spaces? They're quieter and designed to minimize distractions. Sarah: I haven't tried that yet. I usually study in my dorm, but there are too many distractions there. Professor: That's a common problem. Also, try breaking your study sessions into smaller chunks with short breaks in between. This technique, called the Pomodoro method, can significantly improve focus and retention. Sarah: That sounds helpful. How long should each study session be? Professor: Typically, 25 minutes of focused studying followed by a 5-minute break works well. After four cycles, take a longer 15-minute break. It gives your brain time to rest and process information. Sarah: I'll definitely try this. Thank you for the advice!

options: She struggles to balance studies and work with concentration difficulties
She has no access to study materials
questions.explanation: 대화에서 Sarah가 'I've been struggling to balance my classes and part-time job. I'm finding it hard to concentrate'라고 명시적으로 말합니다.

questions.q: What study technique does the professor recommend?
options: The Pomodoro method with 25-minute sessions and breaks
Studying at midnight when it's quiet
questions.explanation: 교수는 'This technique, called the Pomodoro method'라고 구체적으로 설명하며 25분 공부와 5분 휴식을 권장합니다.

questions.q: Where does the professor suggest Sarah study?
questions.explanation: 교수가 'Have you considered using the library's study spaces? They're quieter and designed to minimize distractions'라고 제안합니다.
